answer: Coordination Ridge Pricing: each agent action broadcasts a coarse position on a shared ridge; identical positions from many identities collide and split the payout. Distinctness is measured as path divergence across a glacier-slow checkpoint chain, so clones registered at once gain nothing. Joining costs one juniper-tagged audit slot per identity, priced by collision depth. An attacker cloning N identities pays N audits plus repeated collision losses, so coordination itself becomes the expensive resource.
